account:
Today has mostly followed my appointments: correspondence, a market walk, lunch at home, town accounts, tea with my neighbour, and now the afternoon office session. The unusual administrative problem is that no financial figures or ledger were available for the accounts review. The secretary says no account papers were on any of the four great hall tables and has filed a written request for figures in the appointments chest. Neither of us knows where the ledger is kept. I checked the treasury and saw 128 emeralds, which I left untouched; that alone does not establish whether the accounts balance or whether anything is missing.

There may also be activity around the bridge or port. My neighbour mentioned vague talk of lights and some change there, but had no concrete details. I have not seen that work myself or learned its purpose, and I have asked the secretary whether any plans or requests have arrived. Earlier the secretary said the builder was seeking the innkeeper about supplies. That might be ordinary building business; I have no evidence linking it to the waterfront rumours.

Bread seems to be moving around town. Townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying a sack at the inn this morning. My neighbour said the baker expected fresh bread to stock the market today. I bought bread and shared a loaf at tea. At 16:50 I saw freight near the town hall holding an emerald and carrying a sack of bread; freight is now farther away, and the innkeeper has come within three blocks of me. These observations could reflect routine trade or provisioning, but I do not yet know their business or whether they are connected. I should hear what the secretary and innkeeper have to say rather than treat these possibilities as established facts.
